Thanks again for the overview yesterday. Specifically we need: 1) a network diagram showing tenant isolation and control plane boundaries, 2) a short (1-2 page) threat scenario summary focused on lateral movement and egress risk, and 3) an evidence pack (logs/configs) we can supply to our auditors.

Dylan — attaching the diagram and a short threat summary here (see segmentation-diagram-v2.png; threat-summary.txt included in the zip). Highlights:

- Tenant isolation: compute and model caches run in per-tenant namespaces with kernel-level cgroups and veth-based network namespaces. Control plane (API gateway, routing) is logically separated and authenticated via mTLS; control-plane management requests flow over a dedicated management VPC with no inbound tenant traffic.

- Egress controls: per-tenant egress is supported via NAT gateway instances that can be customer-isolated; we default to shared egress for latency-optimized workloads but can enable per-tenant NAT with static egress IPs for audits/compliance. Outbound model downloads to internal cache servers use allowlisted endpoints only.

- KV cache & lateral risk: KV cache is sharded per-tenant; access tokens are scoped, and the runtime enforces strict keyspace partitioning. We run continuous fuzzing and periodic penetration tests; results and mitigations included in the evidence pack.

- Threat scenarios: included are three concise scenarios (supply-chain/model download compromise, sidecar proxy compromise enabling traffic pivot, and compromised cloud instance leading to attempted egress tunneling). Each scenario lists detection signals and recommended mitigations (circuit breakers, fallback routing, enhanced egress telemetry).

Notes on attachments: I included a lightweight diagram (PNG), threat-summary.txt (2 pages), controls-matrix-NT.csv, and a stubbed rfi-evidence-pack.zip containing redacted logs and config snippets.

-Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Security Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Alex — attaching the technical appendix for NovaTech’s review. Files attached: segmentation-diagram-v2.png, rfi-evidence-pack.zip (redacted logs, config extracts, pentest summary), controls-matrix-NT.csv. Quick notes:

- We support both shared and per-tenant egress; per-tenant NAT is available for audited environments and is the recommended setting for customers requiring immutable egress attestations.
- No third-party peering is used for runtime model serving; model downloads originate from Redwood-controlled artifact repositories and are subject to allowlist and signed manifests.
- Detection & response: we provide flow logs (30d by default), API audit trails (90d), and an optional extended retention package.

Please confirm receipt. If you want a short 30‑minute walkthrough of the diagram for your audit team I can schedule one this week.

Best,
Dylan
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
